newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian crude steady, but perception of ample supply.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude steady, but perception of ample supply.

text.p: Asian crude prices were steady on Tuesday, finding support from the halt in the fall of world futures prices, but regional grades remained under pressure.
Tapis was under pressure and traders were talking the spot market premium down to 30 to 50 cents. A producer said it was negotiating for early May barrels and was being shown a bid at plus 50 cents.
Despite strong middle distillate margins in Singapore, Tapis was struggling because of its relative value to other light sweet crudes, like Indonesia grades and West African.
Traders said Minas and Duri was still overhanging the April market, but Pertamina could roll over the barrels to its May market.

One trader said he expected the Minas and Duri markets to remain weak into June. The only immediate rescue could come from Japan, if generators build up stocks ahead of the summer season when air conditioning demand rises.
Otherwise Minas was offered at flat for April and flat to a small premium for May, traders said.
Traders said 450,000 barrels of April Dai Hung was sold at APPI Minas plus 5/10 cents into China after a tender last week.
Most MidEast cargoes were now sold for the May market, although a handful of cargoes were left available.
A European major was left holding an Oman cargo and was offering at MPM -5 cents. But traders said buyers could hold off as the major was unlikely to run it into its European refinery interests.
May trade for regional grades and June trade for MidEast grades was likely to remain weak, traders said.
